modelResponse.episodeSummary: The patient experienced an episode of frequent PVCs with a non-sustained VT run, classified as stable. The event lasted 8 seconds, with a ventricular rate of 78 bpm. The patient is post-operative day 1 after abdominal surgery, taking hydrochlorothiazide and lisinopril. Labs show hypokalemia (3.1 mmol/L) and hypomagnesemia (1.5 mg/dL).
modelResponse.rhythmInterpretation: Authoritative upstream diagnosis: Frequent PVCs with non-sustained VT run. Source: SLM_Eval. The rhythm diagnosis was not generated by the SLM.
modelResponse.clinicalContext: Ventricular ectopy occurred in a post-operative patient on a thiazide diuretic, with evidence of electrolyte abnormalities (low potassium and magnesium). The episode was hemodynamically stable.
modelResponse.mostLikelyEtiology: Electrolyte imbalance (hypokalemia and hypomagnesemia) secondary to diuretic therapy (hydrochlorothiazide) in a post-operative patient.
